name: Hoham
title: King of Hebron
summary: Hoham was the king of Hebron during Joshua's time. He was one of five Amorite kings who formed an alliance to attack Gibeon after the Gibeonites had made peace with Israel. The coalition was defeated by Joshua in the famous battle where God threw large hailstones from heaven and the sun stood still.

keyEvents.title: The Alliance Against Gibeon
keyEvents.description: Hoham joined forces with four other Amorite kings—Adoni-Zedek of Jerusalem, Piram of Jarmuth, Japhia of Lachish, and Debir of Eglon—to punish Gibeon for making peace with Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Siege of Gibeon
keyEvents.description: The five Amorite kings marched up with their armies and camped against Gibeon and made war on the city. The Gibeonites sent word to Joshua at Gilgal, asking for help.

keyEvents.title: Joshua's Victory Through God's Intervention
keyEvents.description: The Lord struck the Amorites with confusion before Israel, and Joshua inflicted a great defeat on them at Gibeon. God threw large hailstones from heaven upon the fleeing enemies, and more died from the hail than from the sword.

keyEvents.title: The Five Kings Hide in the Cave at Makkedah
keyEvents.description: Hoham and the other four kings fled and hid in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua ordered that large stones be rolled in front of the cave's opening to keep them trapped while the pursuit of the enemy continued.

keyEvents.title: Execution of the Kings
keyEvents.description: After the enemy was defeated, the five kings were brought out of the cave. Joshua had his commanders place their feet on the kings' necks as a sign of complete victory. Then the kings were killed and hung on five trees.
